text:
Matvei Gridin is 20 and already the kind of forward the Flames can build a power play around. He has 14 points in 27 games, five of them with the man advantage, and Calgary is better with him on the ice: 51.5% of five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), and a relative rating of +6.6 against his teammates.

The recent stretch is quieter. Four points in ten games against 5.9 expected, and his last two nights came in at 12.2 and 11.2 minutes, his lightest usage of the month. That's worth watching more than the point total. Sportsnaut has already made the case that Ryan Huska should keep him with Matt Coronato, and our similarity numbers agree the two play alike: they both shoot from distance.

His skating is real, 93rd percentile top speed by NHL EDGE, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 61% of his entries last season (a small sample, eight games). Drafted 28th in 2024, he's at 0.52 points a game; forwards picked around him have usually managed 0.35 in their first full year.
